response.sql:
WITH status_avgs AS (
  SELECT t.equipstatus, AVG(s.pulsepersec) as avg_pulse_rate
  FROM signals s
  INNER JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry
  WHERE s.pulsepersec IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY t.equipstatus
),
first_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_pulse_rate) as mean_val FROM status_avgs
),
filtered_1 AS (
  SELECT sa.equipstatus, sa.avg_pulse_rate
  FROM status_avgs sa
  CROSS JOIN first_mean fm
  WHERE sa.avg_pulse_rate > fm.mean_val
),
second_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_pulse_rate) as mean_val FROM filtered_1
),
filtered_2 AS (
  SELECT f1.avg_pulse_rate,
    f1.avg_pulse_rate - fm.mean_val as excess_first,
    f1.avg_pulse_rate - sm.mean_val as excess_second
  FROM filtered_1 f1
  CROSS JOIN first_mean fm
  CROSS JOIN second_mean sm
  WHERE f1.avg_pulse_rate > sm.mean_val
)
SELECT AVG(avg_pulse_rate), AVG(excess_first), AVG(excess_second) FROM filtered_2

assumptions.assumption: "above the mean" means strictly greater than (>), not ≥. The English word "above" typically denotes strict inequality in mathematical contexts, but this could be interpreted either way.

alternatives.interpretation: "above the mean" could mean ≥ instead of >, including statuses with averages equal to the respective means in both filters.
